# Tracepad

> LLM observability and evals in a single binary — traces, prompts, datasets, scores and review queues for LLM and agent apps, self-hosted.

Every page below is Markdown, and `llms-full.txt` beside this file is all of them in one. These addresses follow the newest release; a version's own pages are under `https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/<version>/` (`dev` is the tip of `main`).

A coding agent setting Tracepad up for a project starts at [Agent setup](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/agent-setup.md).

## Overview

- [Home](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/index.md): Tracepad is LLM observability and evals in a single binary: traces, prompt versions, datasets and eval runs, scores and annotation queues for LLM and agent applications, self-hosted on one embedded…

## Get started

- [Quickstart](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/quickstart.md): From nothing to a trace on screen.
- [Agent setup](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/agent-setup.md): This page is an instruction to a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any other) that a person has asked to set Tracepad up for the project in front of it.
- [Installing the binary](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/install.md): The release archives are one file each and need nothing installed beside them.
- [Docker](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/docker.md): `ghcr.io/tracepad/tracepad` is the server, the web interface and the CLI in one image — the same binary the release archives carry, built from the `Dockerfile` in this repository.
- [Configuration](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/configuration.md): Every variable the server, the CLI and the packages read, in one place.
- [How Tracepad compares](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/compare.md): Tracepad is one way to keep the traces and evals of an LLM application.

## Send traces

- [Sending traces](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/ingest.md): Tracepad speaks OTLP.
- [Python package](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/sdk-python.md): `tracepad` is a thin layer of ergonomics over the OpenTelemetry SDK.
- [Node package](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/sdk-js.md): `tracepad` is a thin layer of ergonomics over the OpenTelemetry JS SDK.
- [Go package](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/sdk-go.md): `tracepad` is a thin layer of ergonomics over the OpenTelemetry Go SDK.
- [Media](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/media.md): A multimodal call sends the model a picture, and the trace of that call keeps what was sent.
- [Coming from the Langfuse SDK](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/langfuse-sdk.md): Tracepad accepts traces from the Langfuse SDK on the route the SDK already uses, `POST /api/public/otel/v1/traces`.

## Use it

- [Web interface](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/ui.md): A browser client of the read API, served by the same binary on the same port.
- [Scores](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/scores.md): A score is a quality judgement attached to a trace, an observation or a session: a number from an eval run, a pass/fail from a guardrail, a verdict from an LLM judge, a rating from a human reviewer.
- [Prompts](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/prompts.md): Tracepad stores prompts as versioned, labelled artefacts.
- [Datasets and runs](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/datasets.md): An eval is a set of cases, a pass over them, and a comparison against last time.
- [Annotation queues](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/annotation.md): Scoring the trace you happen to be reading is one thing.
- [Quality](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/quality.md): A score lives on one trace.
- [Users](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/users.md): A user id rides on most production traces, and until now the store could filter by it, erase by it, and nothing else.

## Read it back

- [Read API](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/api.md): Everything tracepad knows is readable over HTTP.
- [CLI](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/cli.md): The same binary that runs the server is also its client.
- [MCP](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/mcp.md): Tracepad serves the Model Context Protocol so an agent can read traces as tools rather than as HTTP.
- [Coding agents](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/agents.md): A coding agent can reach everything Tracepad has without help: the CLI answers in JSON when piped, the MCP server is in the binary, and `GET /api/v1` describes every route.
- [Taking the data out](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/export.md): Tracepad keeps every export body it accepts, byte for byte, exactly as the client sent it.

## Operate it

- [Accounts](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/accounts.md): People sign in; programs use keys.
- [Administration](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/admin.md): Projects, API keys, retention windows and user-data erasure, over the same JSON API as everything else and through the same binary's CLI.
- [Retention](https://tracepad.github.io/tracepad/dev/retention.md): A store that only grows is a store you eventually delete by hand.
